The N = 48 ED spectrum used approximately 25 million CPU hours which was possible thanks to an overall 40 million CPU hours grant from PRACE. || Acknowledgments: We acknowledge PRACE for granting access to HPC resources at TGCC/CEA under grant number 2019204846SC. SC also acknowledges the use of HPC resources from CALMIP (grants 2021-P0677 and 2022-P0677) and GENCI (grant x2021050225).

compute.note: Worklist row cites the journal URL (PRX 14, 021010) = arXiv:2303.01585 (Wietek, Capponi & Laeuchli). The ~25 million CPU hours is one blanket figure for the entire N = 48 space-group- and spin-parity-resolved ED spectrum at J2/J1 = 0.125, i.e. for all 48 symmetry-sector energies in this worklist together, not per sector. No per-sector run time, core count, memory, Hilbert-space dimension or Lanczos iteration count is stated. Machine is identified only as PRACE HPC resources at TGCC/CEA (CPU). The paper plots only (E - E0)/J1 (Fig. 2(b), Fig. 5(a), Fig. 6(b)); the absolute sector energies are the first author's VarBench deposits (ground state 2022-02-11, 7277cf5; all 48 sectors PR #10, 4aa5e29, 2024-07-29).
